explanation: The pole reads the token it lands on (37% of the input attribution is on the peak token, 28% on the token before it, and token identity explains 77% of the activation variance) and fires retrospectively when that token opens a concrete English content word - a physical object or part (blanket, curtain, umbrella, barrier, anchor, brake, base, chain, body, head, palm), a simple posture/motion verb (stand, stood, sat, sitting, waiting, stopped, riding, bending) - or the first fragment of a rare name or technical word (Al-, al-, sat-, carb-, hydroxide, chromatography, lua, hljs). It stays at or below the activity line on function words, on high-frequency generic and abstract nouns (place, city, effect, notion, factor, answer, description), on -tion/-ment/-ness/-ity nominalizations and on the most frequent tokens of the corpus, which essentially never fire (in a 200k-token replay of this pole, 1 of 12,766 occurrences of tokens seen 160-400 times in the corpus and 26 of 66,406 above 400 reached the activity line), while a minority of rare concrete nouns (quill, loom, plough, trellis, trowel) is also silent - so the class is a graded lexical neighbourhood, not a closed WordNet category; the negative pole is only the GELU floor (max 0.17, 74% of tokens above a quarter of it) and the Jacobian lens's promoted newline/indent tokens are not realised as a next-token target under ablation (KL 0.02, no concentrated token set), so the pole's job is reading the peak token, not preparing the next one.
